name: exomizer
desc: File compressor optimized for decompression in 8-bit environments
why: A compressor built for 8-bit decompression, a glimpse into retro demoscene and constrained-machine engineering.

brief.what_it_is: Exomizer is a file compressor, per its Homebrew description, optimized so the compressed data can be decompressed on 8-bit machines. The formula installs two executables, exomizer and exobasic. I could not read the project's own description of inputs and outputs, so this entry relies on the Homebrew summary.
brief.why_it_exists: The Homebrew description says it is built for decompression in 8-bit environments. The project's own stated reasoning was not visible to me.
brief.install_notes: Nothing beyond brew install was visible. The formula lists the executables exobasic and exomizer. I saw no notes on runtimes, accounts, or first-run setup.
brief.standout: Per the scout notes, it is a compressor built for 8-bit decompression, tied to retro demoscene and constrained-machine engineering. I could not confirm this from the project's pages.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage loaded only as an empty Bitbucket page shell, with no README text, release date, or commit information visible. The guessed README path and the wiki/Home page also gave no usable content, and the wiki returned a 404.
brief.caveats: The Bitbucket homepage and the guessed README path returned no project content, so this brief rests on the Homebrew description and scout notes alone. Nothing about platform support, licensing, build steps, or limits could be verified. The exobasic executable is not explained anywhere I could read.
